findings: Native snapshots require explicit stopped metadata, native-json-v1, basename-only saved path, exact settled head, hash and private owned regular file. Legacy RPC snapshot guard is unchanged. No automatic admission of the historical running record.

Native file hashing is streaming, no-follow, checks inode and in-flight size/mtime/ctime. Fresh output path differs from immutable load input. After native load, input hash and actual L1 head/hash/pending/proven must match before node services.

Clean shutdown drains mining/RPC, settles and stops node, captures settled L1 head, requires clean Anvil exit, then hashes native output and records stopped metadata. Any preceding cleanup failure prevents qualification; an old periodic output cannot serve after restart unless exact head verification succeeds.

2 GiB native JSON capacity is separate from unchanged 128 MiB legacy representation limit. Actual memory capacity remains bounded by runtime owners; the measured saved 1.147 GB file loaded within 4 GiB.

MetaMask worker exemption is test-only GET, exact official version and worker URL, finite static filenames, absent query or fixed Workbox revision syntax, and requires previously verified extension startup frame. Application warning navigations are not admitted. Retained profile explicitly waits for authentic unlock.

Refresh observation keeps original locks, context guards, PXE sync, initialization, method return and exact thrown values. Five-field projection admits only fixed method/phase/code labels, rejects accessors, absorbs observer errors, and clears account-invalidated observations. It grants no readiness authority.
Exact Design266 four source hashes and two receipt/log pairs match current candidate. Source-bound 11 unit and three local DOM checks are labelled fixtures, not proof of historical runtime cause.

Current manifest input and SDK/apps/wallet output hashes rechecked directly with zero mismatches. Normal build owner ran existing SDK/apps/wallet builders successfully; no manual generated rewrite identified.
